headline: Sequence foundation models spread across DNA, RNA and protein as evaluation gets stricter
label: Biological Sequence Foundation Models
summary: New RNA and DNA pretraining (structRFM, LIMBER, IsoAlign) arrives alongside work exposing homology leakage, ligand invariance, and uncalibrated PLM scores.
synthesis: The dominant thread is pretraining sequence representations and reusing them for downstream prediction across DNA, RNA, and protein. On the nucleic-acid side, structRFM is pre-trained on 21M sequence-structure pairs and LIMBER, a hybrid self-attention/Mamba model, on 40.5M ncRNA sequences. IsoAlign pretrains DNA models through isoform-aware DNA-protein alignment with JEPA objectives, and TriTower-m6Am fuses RNA-FM embeddings with sequential and structural towers. For proteins, MaskNGly uses PLM embeddings zero-shot for N-glycosylation sites and matches supervised predictors. PALM adapts ESM2 with LoRA and a BiLSTM for domain, functional-site, and missense-effect prediction. What is newer is scrutiny of reliability. Protify reports task dependence and homology leakage in PLM benchmarks. PPI-Caliper applies conformal calibration to control false discovery rate in PLM interaction scores without retraining. A MET kinase deep mutational scanning benchmark across 11 inhibitors finds current models largely ligand-invariant.
